surface_mechanism_description: The surface reaction mechanism involves the chemisorption of vanadyl triisopropoxide (VO(OPr_i)3) onto surface hydroxyl groups (Si-OH*) of silica, forming a surface-bound vanadate species (VO-O-Si*). Subsequent reaction with water (H2O) regenerates surface hydroxyl groups (Si-OH) and produces isopropoxide ligands (Pr_i-OH).
evidence: The surface reaction mechanism was discussed in the context of the chemisorption of vanadyl triisopropoxide onto silica surfaces, as described in the text: 'The controlled and reproducible chemisorption-based growth of vanadia on silica occurred in a temperature range from 363 to 393 K... The precursor deposition progressed via both mono- and bidentate surface species... The reaction between VO(OPr_i)3 and silica pretreated at 873 K was investigated... The surface site saturation of silica both at the top and at the bottom parts of the support bed was seen from the consumption of the free Si-OH groups... The surface site saturation of silica both at the top and at the bottom parts of the support bed was seen from the consumption of the free Si-OH groups at 3745 cm-1 and 980 cm-1... The surface site saturation of silica both at the top and at the bottom parts of the support bed was seen from the consumption of the free Si-OH groups at 3745 cm-1 and 980 cm-1 (Figure 2, parts A, samples a -c, and B, samples a-c).'
